messages:
sahil: FYI ran the kernel+driver bump on a 6-node canary fleet in us-west2 an hour ago: kernel 6.5.15 -> 6.6.2, nvidia 540.47 -> 550.19. Seeing an Xid spike on 2 cards across 2 hosts.

ops-bot: xid-spike-detector alert: metric 'xid_33_count' exceeded threshold (window=5m) on host gpu-wst-canary-03, gpu0 and gpu2.

joyce: can you paste the dmesg/Xid lines? also which firmware revision?

sahil: firmware on affected cards is 52.34.0 (same as cluster baseline). dmesg snippet below:

```
[Aug 12 17:12:45] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 33, PID 4217, 0x00000003
[Aug 12 17:12:45] nvrm: RmProbe failed on GPU 0: Xid 33
[Aug 12 17:12:46] kernel: NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus: disconnecting
[Aug 12 17:12:46] kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: GPU reported ECC error count increase
```

maria: that looks like the same symptom we saw in feb smoke where the newer driver exposed a timing race with kernel 6.6 on certain firmware. Did we run the stress microbench for >30m?

sahil: we ran the standard preflight 10m stress + 5m sustained throughput (squeezenet workload). Only 2/6 nodes hit errors but both had sustained 98% util on gpu0 for multiple minutes.

joyce: upload of the full telemetry is in the canary bucket: s3://redwood-canary/us-west2/1843000000-post-upgrade/ - includes: gpu-events.json, dmesg.log, nvidia-smi-samples.csv.

ops-bot: telemetry ingestion complete. Regression check: xid-rate increased by 4.6x vs baseline for canary window.

oncall-lead: tagging this P1 for the oncall rotation. Please freeze further rollouts to staging/dedicated until triage completes.

maria: quick triage checklist: 1) confirm reproducibility under synthetic memtest, 2) confirm ECC counts persist after soft-reset, 3) try kernel 6.6.2 + driver 540.47 (old driver) to narrow which component regressed.

joyce: I kicked off a memtest job with ECC stress (job id memtest-184300). Also launched a repro pod pinned to gpu-wst-canary-03:gpu0 with `nvidia-smi --auto-burn` loop.

sahil: results so far: memtest show ECC counters tick on gpu0 at ~3 errors/hour under mem-stress. soft-reset (`nvidia-smi -r`) temporarily clears the Xid burst but it returns within 12 minutes.

joyce: tried the rollback matrix: kernel 6.5.15 + driver 550.19 = no repro so far. kernel 6.6.2 + driver 540.47 = repro persists. that points to kernel-driver interaction where the newer kernel + newer driver together cause faster failure but kernel seems main vector.

maria: good isolate. Can we snapshot the exact kernel config bits (CONFIG_HYPERV etc) and check if we pulled any backported patches? Also check the ABI/PCI power management changes.

sahil: pulling `uname -a` and kernel config: `Linux gpu-wst-canary-03 6.6.2-redwood+ #12 SMP PREEMPT Tue Aug 11` — uploaded config at s3 path above.

ops-bot: automatic note: capacity impact estimate: 2 nodes partially degraded (~12% effective GPU capacity loss) during canary. No customer impact in hosted region yet.

oncall-lead: next actions proposed: 1) pause rollout to us-east and eu (done), 2) expand canary to 12 nodes but only run synthetic low-util tests (no high sustained util) to gather more telemetry, 3) open driver vendor ticket with logs + repro job, 4) schedule rollback of kernel to 6.5.15 on canary if we see >5% nodes repro in next 6h.

joyce: I'll run expanded canary with a two-tier stress matrix (short burst 95% util, long tail 60% util) and share telemetry. starting at 1843000065.

sahil: for remediation, if rollback is needed exec commands: `kubectl drain gpu-wst-canary-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data && ./infra/node-reimage --kernel=6.5.15 --driver=540.47 --host=gpu-wst-canary-03` (we have automation in infra repo).

maria: also add a temporary alert rule with lower threshold for xid_33 across all canaries so we catch recurrence quicker.

joyce: vendor ticket opened (NV-84721) with attached telemetry + repro job. assigned to driver-eng.

ops-bot: note added to incident timeline: vendor ticket NV-84721, rollback threshold set at 5% nodes.

sahil: tagging @infra-sig for reimage window if rollback required. Also - ops ask: should we disable aggressive power-saving (pstate/power limit) on canary during tests? it was enabled cluster-wide last month.

maria: yes temporarily set `--gpu-power-save=off` for repro runs, might change thermal/timing profile. Add to test matrix.

oncall-lead: summary: hold rollout, expanded telemetry, vendor engaged, rollback plan ready. I'll follow up in 4h with decision or earlier if repro crosses threshold. :thumbsup:

joyce: will post updated telemetry link and short repro video when available.

sahil: thanks all, will keep this thread updated.
